name: Phinehas
overview: Phinehas was a male member of the tribe of Levi, serving as a High Priest. He was uniquely identified as Eleazar's son and Aaron's grandson, a lineage that established his prominent priestly role. God granted him a covenant of peace and a perpetual priesthood, underscoring his lasting significance in Israel's religious leadership.
namesAndTitles: The name Phinehas, meaning 'the black man,' is his proper name as recorded in Exodus 6:25. This name was not given by God but is the one by which he is known in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Phinehas was the son of Eleazar and the father of Abishua, placing him firmly within the priestly lineage descending from Aaron. He is also connected ancestrally to Gershom and Eleazar as noted in Ezra, indicating his heritage within the Levitical family.
scriptureSignificance: Phinehas holds a vital place in the biblical narrative as a High Priest who received a divine covenant promising peace and an enduring priesthood. This covenant highlights God's approval of his zeal and faithfulness, ensuring his descendants' ongoing role in leading Israel's worship and maintaining covenant faithfulness. His priestly service reflects the continuation of Aaron's legacy through his lineage.
